title: Make selected-missing failure posture explicit and configurable

state.decision_rationale: Accepted and completed in MKTCTX/5: --missing=error|record governs output and exit behavior, stable structured diagnostics cover every omission class, and verification reports integrity, completeness, and policy compliance separately.

provenance.review_target: Reported 396-file MKTCTX/3 packet with 46 selected-missing paths; exact artifact not identified

feedback.verbatim: Make missing selected files louder. In an archival packet, emitting the packet with omissions is fine. In a code-review or CI packet, 46 selected-missing entries should probably produce @diagnostic severity=error code=SELECTED_FILE_MISSING and @packet valid=false unless the caller explicitly supplied allow_missing=true. The current transparency is excellent; the failure posture needs to be configurable.
feedback.normalized_claim: Add explicit diagnostic severity, packet validity, and caller-controlled missing-file policy rather than treating every omission as a warning-compatible packet.

current_behavior: Explicit --files-from selection is strict and exits on a missing or non-file path before writing output.
Implicit piped selection warns, skips missing and non-file paths, emits the packet when at least one usable file remains, and records omissions with selected_complete=false.
Packets have no valid field, diagnostic severity, or allow_missing policy declaration.
evidence: src/index.test.ts: strict and implicit missing-path tests

proposal.summary: Evaluate a declared omission policy and structured diagnostics so archival, interactive, review, and CI uses can choose different failure postures.
candidate_changes: Add CLI policy such as --missing=error|record or --allow-missing with an explicit packet field recording the chosen policy.
Add structured @diagnostic records with severity, code, path, and detail.
Add packet validity only after defining whether validity means parseable, policy-compliant, complete for selection, or safe for a named workflow.
Consider emitting a packet and returning nonzero in CI mode so diagnostics remain inspectable.
non_goals: Do not silently downgrade explicit strict selection.
Do not make valid=false an overloaded substitute for precise coverage and diagnostics.
Do not assume every Git deletion is an error when the caller intentionally selected final-worktree files.

questions: Should policy defaults depend on explicit manifest, implicit stdin, discovery, or a named profile?
Can a packet be useful and structurally valid while violating a caller completeness policy?
Should binary, invalid UTF-8, directories, and output-file exclusions share the same severity policy as missing files?
How should process exit status relate to emitted packet validity?
risks: A packet-level valid boolean may collapse multiple independent validity dimensions.
Failing on Git deletion paths could recreate the original unusable pipe workflow.
Emitting output on a nonzero exit can surprise shell pipelines unless documented carefully.
evidence_needed: Workflow matrix for archival, interactive review, CI, and retrieval use.
Fixtures and expected exit/output behavior for each omission reason and policy.
Model tests comparing plain omissions with structured diagnostics.
CLI compatibility analysis for the existing strict and implicit modes.
